senses.sense_definition: To write down or type out spoken language from live speech or an audio recording.

examples.text: The secretary spent the entire morning helping to <w>transcribe</w> the recorded interviews.
The doctor made several recordings today which she will <w>transcribe</w> into medical reports tomorrow.

senses.sense_definition: To arrange or rewrite a musical composition for a different instrument or voice, or to write down recorded music into notation.

examples.text: He decided to <w>transcribe</w> the famous piano piece for classical guitar.
She was able to listen to the jazz solo and quickly <w>transcribe</w> it onto sheet music.

senses.sense_definition: To represent speech sounds using a specialized phonetic alphabet or symbols.

examples.text: Linguists often use the International Phonetic Alphabet to <w>transcribe</w> unfamiliar dialects.
The researcher had to carefully <w>transcribe</w> each vowel sound produced by the speakers.

senses.sense_definition: To transfer data or electronic information from one recording medium or format to another.

examples.text: Engineers worked diligently to <w>transcribe</w> the magnetic tape data onto modern digital drives.
The archive plans to <w>transcribe</w> all legacy storage files before the hardware fails.

senses.sense_definition: To synthesize RNA using a DNA sequence as a template.

examples.text: Enzymes in the cell nucleus help <w>transcribe</w> specific genes into messenger RNA.
RNA polymerase is the primary enzyme that helps <w>transcribe</w> genetic sequences.
